summary: Iteration 33 (backend-only): verified streaming-insert pipeline, chunked branch_transfer (fix for latent 0-record bug), replace+undo chunked backup, attempts=3 exhaustion, unknown 404, and AUTO-RESUME after SIGKILL. All 6 pytest cases pass (test_streaming_pipeline_iter33.py). Auto-resume proof: 26MB/300K-row sale upload was killed at t+4.5s (fuser -k -9 8001/tcp + pkill spawn + supervisorctl restart); status endpoint surfaced 'Resuming after server restart...' at t+92s (past 90s stale threshold) and final status='complete' with EXACTLY 300000 records at t+110s (0 duplicates, upload_chunks cleaned). DB restored to baseline (total_transactions=11767).

critical_code_review_comments: Streaming pipeline in _process_upload (server.py:1386-1414) is clean: batched flush every 5000 records via run_coroutine_threadsafe keeps memory bounded; batch_id assigned before inserts enables clean rollback.
_choose_excel_reader/_iter_excel_rows uses cgroup headroom for calamine-vs-openpyxl decision; sensible with a 30x compressed-size expansion heuristic + 150MB safety margin.

_try_resume_upload atomic claim (conditional attempt writes) + rollback-by-batch_id + replay-from-stored-chunks is the right shape. Confirmed 3-trigger recovery (startup, 120s sweep, status-poll) — status poll fired at t+92s in test.

Suggestion (nice-to-have, not blocking): the stale-heartbeat/attempts-exhausted parse still uses `except ValueError:` on datetime.fromisoformat (server.py ~line 1409 area). If heartbeat is ever stored non-string, TypeError would leak. Consider `except (ValueError, TypeError)`. Same suggestion as iter32.
server.py at 7625 lines — the upload/session subsystem (~500-600 lines) is a natural extraction candidate into services/uploads.py to reduce cognitive load.
